## Class activity: Poisson regression assumptions

```{r, echo=F, message=FALSE, warning=F, fig.align='center', fig.width=3.5, fig.height=3}
library(tidyverse)
library(statmod)
library(topmodels)
library(gridExtra)

set.seed(1)
r <- 0.5
n <- 1000
x <- rnorm(n, sd = 0.5)
y1 <- rpois(n, lambda = exp(x))
y2 <- rpois(n, lambda = exp(x^2))
y3 <- rnbinom(n, size=r, mu=exp(x))
y4 <- rnbinom(n, size=r, mu=exp(x^2))

m1 <- glm(y1 ~ x, family = poisson)
m2 <- glm(y2 ~ x, family = poisson)
m3 <- glm(y3 ~ x, family = poisson)
m4 <- glm(y4 ~ x, family = poisson)

p1 <- data.frame(x = x, resids = qresid(m1)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = x, y = resids)) +
  geom_point(size=0.3) +
  geom_smooth() +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(x = "X", y = "Quantile residuals", 
       title = "Poisson data, \n shape assumption satisfied") +
  scale_y_continuous(limits=c(-3, 6)) +
  theme(text = element_text(size = 6))
p2 <- data.frame(x = x, resids = qresid(m2)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = x, y = resids)) +
  geom_point(size=0.3) +
  geom_smooth() +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(x = "X", y = "Quantile residuals", 
       title = "Poisson data, \n shape assumption violated") +
  scale_y_continuous(limits=c(-3, 6)) +
  theme(text = element_text(size = 6))
p3 <- data.frame(x = x, resids = qresid(m3)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = x, y = resids)) +
  geom_point(size=0.3) +
  geom_smooth() +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(x = "X", y = "Quantile residuals", 
       title = "Non-Poisson data, \n shape assumption satisfied") +
  scale_y_continuous(limits=c(-3, 6)) +
  theme(text = element_text(size = 6))
p4 <- data.frame(x = x, resids = qresid(m4)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = x, y = resids)) +
  geom_point(size=0.3) +
  geom_smooth() +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(x = "X", y = "Quantile residuals", 
       title = "Non-Poisson data, \n shape assumption violated") +
  scale_y_continuous(limits=c(-3, 6)) +
  theme(text = element_text(size = 6))

grid.arrange(p1, p2, p3, p4, ncol=2)
```


## Using quantile residual plots

All assumptions are satisfied:

* Residuals are randomly scattered around 0, with no clear pattern
* Residuals have constant variance
* Residuals are mostly between -2 and 2

If you see a pattern in the residuals:

* Shape assumption may not be satisfied

If residuals have non-constant variance, and/or variance is too large:

* Distribution assumption may not be satisfied


## Rootograms

```{r, echo=F, fig.width=4, fig.height=3, fig.align="center"}
rootogram(m1)
```

## Examining rootograms

```{r, echo=F, fig.width=4, fig.height=3}
rootogram(m3)
```

## QQ plots

When the model assumptions are satisfied:

```{r, echo=F, fig.width=4, fig.height=3}
data.frame(resids = qresid(m1)) |>
  ggplot(aes(sample = resids)) +
  geom_qq() +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, 
              color = "orange") +
  labs(x = "Theoretical normal quantiles",
       y = "Observed residual quantiles") +
  theme_bw()
```

## QQ plots

When the model assumptions are not satisfied:

```{r, echo=F, fig.width=4, fig.height=3, warning=F}
data.frame(resids = qresid(m2)) |>
  ggplot(aes(sample = resids)) +
  geom_qq() +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, 
              color = "orange") +
  labs(x = "Theoretical normal quantiles",
       y = "Observed residual quantiles") +
  theme_bw()
```
